events.text: [LESSON_START] The current lesson workspace is mounted. Call observe_runtime for its task and ongoing state updates, then teach naturally.

task.task: Put two counters on the frame. Your turn.

demand.constraints: The learner answers on the frame. The frame checks the placement once the learner stops.

levers.when: The learner miscounts while placing: one too many, one too few, or loses track.
levers.does: Shows under the frame how many counters the learner has placed so far. Never the number to build.

levers.when: The learner counts one by one and loses track past five.
levers.does: Outlines the top row of the frame and marks it 5, so the learner can count on from a full row.

levers.when: The learner cannot build a number this big yet.
levers.does: Opens an easier build first, about half as many counters. It is not graded; the full item comes back after it.

choices.description: Pull one lever from workspace.levers on this item when the learner is stuck: pick the one whose "when" fits why. It changes the screen and is recorded as help. Supply lever: its id. Wait for the visible result, then say what changed, in your own words, and let the learner try. A simplify lever opens an easier practice item first; the full item comes back after it.

Begin a teaching exchange in words only. Records assistance without submitting an answer. No parameters. When the learner is stuck on this item, use pull_lever instead: it changes the screen and records the help itself.

items.hint: Count slowly as you place two red counters on the top row.
items.narration: Let us start by putting 2 counters on the ten frame.
items.instruction: Put 2 counters on the ten frame!

items.hint: Fill the first four spaces starting from the top left.
items.narration: Now, let us build the number 4.
items.instruction: Put 4 counters on the ten frame!
